internal_alignment: Order three objects by length; compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object; express the length of an object as a whole number of same-size length units laid end to end with no gaps or overlaps. Internal record only; no standards codes appear on any child page, and no separate answer key is published for this pack.
model_accuracy: Unit is one paper clip throughout. Page 1 uses enlarged clips (40 by 20 points): pencil span 160 points equals exactly 4 clips; Panel A clips start and end exactly with the pencil (asserted at build time); Panel B has an 8-point gap between clips 2 and 3; Panel C overlaps clips 2 and 3 by 16 points; Panel D mixes 52-point and 28-point units. Page 2 counts, each asserted to end exactly with its object: Ribbon 6, Pencil 4, Crayon 8, Straw 5, all distinct. Page 3 worked example: ribbon 5 units, rope 7 units, gold strip exactly 5 units in both appearances, never two lengths. Page 3 activity: scarf 4 units starting at x=170 and ending at 282; belt 3 units starting at x=230 and ending at 314, so the belt ends further right yet is shorter; the same 4-unit strip aligned to each start (170-282 for the scarf, 230-342 for the belt) shows the scarf is longer. Page 4 counts, each asserted: Ribbon A 6 clips order 3 (longest), Ribbon B 3 clips order 1 (shortest), Ribbon C 5 clips order 2 (middle). Page 5 is hands-on with real clips, so counts vary with the real objects; the longest object is the one that took the most clips.
pack: Grade 1 Math: Comparing and Measuring Lengths

pages_detail.activities: Four clearly separated answer panels (A-D) showing the same large pencil measured four ways; circle the panel that measures the pencil correctly
answers: Panel A: correct, same-size clips touching end to end, starting and ending with the pencil
pages_detail.title: Which Measurement Is Right?

pages_detail.activities: Count the paper clips under each illustrated object and write the count in the box
pages_detail.title: Measure with Paper Clips

pages_detail.activities: Worked example: gold strip matched to the ribbon, then the same strip falls short of the rope; activity: same strip aligned to the staggered starts of a scarf and a belt; circle the Scarf or Belt answer panel
answers: Worked example: the rope is longer
Activity: the scarf is longer (belt ends further right but is shorter)
pages_detail.title: Compare Without Moving

pages_detail.activities: Count the clips for three staggered ribbons, write each count, then write 1 for the shortest, 2 for the middle, and 3 for the longest; closing check: tick the true sentence
answers: True sentence: the longest ribbon has the most paper clips
pages_detail.title: Order Three by Length

pages_detail.activities: Hands-on: measure a real pencil, spoon, and book with real same-size paper clips end to end with no gaps and no overlaps; record each count; circle the longest object among three choice panels
answers: Counts vary with the real objects used
Longest object: the one that took the most paper clips
pages_detail.title: Measure for Real
